title: Fallforward hotfix orchestration and customer escalation flow for model rollout regressions
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Context: Recent rollouts of v1.23 model variants exposed a class of regressions that only appear under production traffic mixes (longer tail prompts, multi-turn KV access patterns) in Hosted and Dedicated customers; a private deployment reported similar behavior after orchestration applied the same model bundle. This ticket defines a playbook for fast mitigation (fallforward + hotfix), coordinated customer escalations, and a deterministic post-incident workflow.

Goal: Provide a single, actionable incident lifecycle that reduces MTTI and customer downtime by standardizing: detection thresholds, triage ownership, fallforward and hotpatch creation, cross-environment promotion rules, and customer communications. The playbook must work for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments with minimal divergence and clear lift/rollback criteria.
acceptance_criteria:
- A documented runbook that on-call SREs and triage engineers can execute within 30 minutes for a canary-quality regression.
- Templates for customer communication and support handoff added to the incident playbook.
- Automation (scripts/CLI) to pin a fallforward variant or apply a hotpatch to Hosted/Dedicated control planes.
- Validation checks for Private customers (pre-approved hotpatch artifacts and signed manifests) documented.
- Postmortem checklist and follow-up action tracker created and linked.
runbook_steps:
1) Detection: Alert triggers when canary failure rate > 2% over 10 minutes OR production quality regression score delta > configured threshold.
2) Initial Triage: Assign on-call SRE and model owner. Reproduce issue in canary and a synthetic replay environment. Capture failing traces, top prompts, and KV cache usage.
3) Impact Assessment: Determine scope by environment (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) and affected model variants. Classify as: widespread customer-facing, tiered degradation, or isolated experiment.
4) Short-term mitigation (Fallforward): If regression is model-induced, fallforward to the most recent compatible model variant or inference config (lower quantization, disable experimental kernel) that preserves API contract. Use automated routing policy to pin traffic away from the regressing variant.
5) Hotfix path: If fallforward cannot be applied or preserves unacceptable quality loss, create a hotpatch: minimal model/config change or runtime flag toggle that addresses failing code path. Ship hotpatch to Hosted first, verify canary, then Dedicated reserved pools, then coordinate with Private customers for signed hotpatch artifacts.
6) Coordination: Use the orchestration channel (pager and #inc-rollouts) to publish status, action, and owner. For Private customers, trigger the pre-approved upgrade flow and provide signed manifests and validation steps.
7) Verification: Run a graduated canary (1%, 10%, 50%) with synthetic and sampled production traffic. Compare quality metrics and latency impact.
8) Rollback fallback: If the patch worsens metrics, immediately revert to the pinned fallforward variant and escalate to engineering leads for hotpatch iteration.
9) Customer closure: Send templated update to affected customers with timeline, root cause hypothesis, and follow-up plan.
10) Post-incident: Complete RCA, add regression tests to the model onboarding pipeline, and schedule follow-ups in the release cadence.
communication_plan:
Channels: PagerDuty for on-call, #inc-rollouts Slack for cross-team coordination, #cust-escalations for customer comms.
Templates: - Initial notice (what we’ve observed, immediate mitigation being applied, ETA for next update). - Mid-incident update (verification status, next steps). - Resolution message (root cause hypothesis, artifacts, and remediation).
Stakeholders to notify: Support, Sales AE, Customer Success, Security (if customer data exposure suspected), and Legal for regulated customers.
Private deployments: Provide signed artifacts and a secure S3 link plus a verification checklist. Offer SRE-to-SRE handoff call within 2 hours of remediation for enterprise customers.
postmortem_actions: Add synthetic replay tests covering KV cache heavy scenarios to CI
Introduce model-variant compatibility checks to onboarding pipeline
Automate fallforward pinning in the control plane with audit logs
Create a dedicated Dedicated/Private escalation checklist and runbook
Schedule quarterly tabletop exercises with Support and Customer Success
notes:
Trade-offs: fallforward reduces blast radius and preserves availability but may degrade user-visible quality. Hotpatches are higher-risk but can fix specific regressions faster. For Private customers, we must balance speed with signed artifact policies and maintenance windows. Decision matrix included in the linked doc.

Open questions: - Do we allow automated fallforward for customers with strict model-version policies? (proposal: opt-in via support agreement). - What SLAs for canary re-verification are reasonable to avoid repeated oscillation?
